name: rsync
description: Efficiently synchronizes files and directories, transferring only the differences, locally or over SSH.

flags.description: Archive mode: recursive, preserves permissions, times, symlinks, owner/group (as root).
--partial --progress: keep partially transferred files and show progress.
Delete files in the destination that no longer exist in the source (makes an exact mirror).
--dry-run: show what would happen without changing anything.
Specify the remote shell (default is ssh anyway).

examples.explanation: Synchronizes project into backup, copying only changed data. NOTE the trailing slashes: project/ copies the contents into backup/; without it, backup/project/ is created.
Mirrors a website to a server over SSH with compression. --delete removes remote files that disappeared locally.
Resumable large-file transfer with a progress bar; re-running continues instead of restarting.
Dry run: lists exactly what would be copied and deleted. Always dry-run first when using --delete.
Backs up a project while skipping heavy, regenerable directories.

about: rsync compares file size and mtime by default (the "quick check") and for changed files transfers only differing blocks via its delta algorithm — dramatically faster than scp for repeated syncs. It preserves almost everything with -a and can run as a daemon, but SSH is the usual transport.
useCases: Mirroring directories and resuming interrupted transfers.
mistakes: Confusing trailing slashes: src and src/ select different data. Test with -n first.
Using --delete without --dry-run and deleting data on the destination that you meant to keep.
warnings: --delete is destructive on the destination. Combine with -n (dry run) before every real run, especially in scripts.
distroNotes: rsync is present on virtually all Linux distributions and macOS. On Windows it runs via WSL or cwRsync.
